copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Monday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Sweden and Tunisia together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Tunisia side, by +12.8pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Public Elo rates Sweden 10 points higher than the other side (Sweden 1660, Tunisia 1650). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Sweden to win at 36%, the draw at 29%, and Tunisia to win at 34%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Sweden to win at 52%, the draw at 28%, and Tunisia to win at 22%. The Tunisia side trades at 22% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +365. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 34%, +12.8pp wider.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Tunisia side that lower bound is 29% — +7.7pp clear of the market's 22%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 23 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Tunisia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.8pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Tunisia side, not a blanket read on the market.
copy.summary: The model thinks Tunisia are mispriced. Our number reads 34% on the away side; the market reads 22%. The +12.8pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: Sweden v Tunisia · the model leans Tunisia
